## User Provider

> **Customize how the current user is identified in audit entries**

A user provider returns information about the current user for audit entries.

### 📝 Interface

```php
namespace DH\Auditor\User;

interface UserProviderInterface
{
    public function __invoke(): ?UserInterface;
}
```

The provider must return a `UserInterface` or `null`:

```php
namespace DH\Auditor\User;

interface UserInterface
{
    public ?string $identifier { get; }

    public ?string $username { get; }

    public ?string $fqdn { get; }                 // class of the user, written as user_fqdn

    public ?UserInterface $impersonator { get; }  // user who impersonates this one (switch user)
}
```

The interface declares read-only property hooks, not getter methods: read `$user->identifier`, `$user->username`,
`$user->fqdn` and `$user->impersonator`.
The built-in `DH\Auditor\User\User` implements it and is what the examples below return.

### 📦 Built-in Provider

The default `DH\AuditorBundle\User\UserProvider`:

- blames the user of the security token: its `getId()` (an empty identifier without that method), its
  `getUserIdentifier()` and its class (Doctrine proxies resolved), written as `user_fqdn`;
- when that user is impersonated (switch user, `SwitchUserToken`), the user of the original token is its
  impersonator, written apart in the `impersonator` key of the `blame` JSON:

```json
{
  "username": "alice",
  "user_fqdn": "App\\Entity\\User",
  "user_firewall": "main",
  "ip": "10.0.0.1",
  "impersonator": {"id": "1", "username": "admin", "fqdn": "App\\Entity\\User"}
}
```

The viewer shows an "impersonated by" badge next to the origin of the action. To find the actions made by
impersonating someone, use the `ImpersonatorFilter` of auditor-doctrine-provider, or `$entry->impersonator`.

> [!NOTE]
> Before 8.0, the built-in provider appended the impersonator to the username (`alice[impersonator admin]`) and
> `user_fqdn` held `DH\Auditor\User\User`. Those entries are not rewritten; the viewer does not show that class.

### 🖥️ Console Commands

For CLI commands, the bundle provides `DH\AuditorBundle\User\ConsoleUserProvider` which automatically tracks the command name:

```php
public function __invoke(): ?UserInterface
{
    if (null === $this->currentCommand) {
        return null;
    }

    // Command name is used as both ID and username
    return new User(
        $this->currentCommand,  // e.g., 'app:import-users'
        $this->currentCommand
    );
}
```

> [!TIP]
> This allows you to:
> - 🔍 Identify which command made specific changes
> - 🔎 Filter audit entries by command in the viewer
> - 📊 Track automated processes separately from user actions

**Example audit entries:**
- `app:import-users` - Import command
- `doctrine:fixtures:load` - Fixtures loading
- `app:sync-products` - Sync command

While a command runs, the console user provider replaces the configured `user_provider`; the configured one is
restored when the command ends.

### 🔧 Creating a Custom Provider

#### Basic Example

```php
<?php

namespace App\Audit;

use DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\Persistence\Helper\DoctrineHelper;
use DH\Auditor\User\User;
use DH\Auditor\User\UserInterface;
use DH\Auditor\User\UserProviderInterface;

class CustomUserProvider implements UserProviderInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly MyAuthService $authService,
    ) {}

    public function __invoke(): ?UserInterface
    {
        $user = $this->authService->getCurrentUser();

        if (null === $user) {
            return null;
        }

        return new User(
            (string) $user->getId(),
            $user->getEmail(),
            DoctrineHelper::getRealClassName($user), // written as user_fqdn, Doctrine proxies resolved
        );
    }
}
```

#### Registration

```yaml
# config/packages/dh_auditor.yaml
dh_auditor:
    user_provider: 'App\Audit\CustomUserProvider'
```

The service is auto-wired. If you need explicit configuration:

```yaml
# config/services.yaml
services:
    App\Audit\CustomUserProvider:
        arguments:
            - '@App\Security\MyAuthService'
```

### 📚 Examples

#### 🔑 API Token Authentication

```php
<?php

namespace App\Audit;

use App\Security\ApiTokenManager;
use DH\Auditor\User\User;
use DH\Auditor\User\UserInterface;
use DH\Auditor\User\UserProviderInterface;

class ApiUserProvider implements UserProviderInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ApiTokenManager $tokenManager,
    ) {}

    public function __invoke(): ?UserInterface
    {
        $token = $this->tokenManager->getCurrentToken();

        if (null === $token) {
            return null;
        }

        return new User(
            $token->getClientId(),
            sprintf('API: %s', $token->getClientName())
        );
    }
}
```

#### 🌐 External OAuth/SSO

```php
<?php

namespace App\Audit;

use DH\Auditor\User\User;
use DH\Auditor\User\UserInterface;
use DH\Auditor\User\UserProviderInterface;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RequestStack;

class OAuthUserProvider implements UserProviderInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly RequestStack $requestStack,
    ) {}

    public function __invoke(): ?UserInterface
    {
        $request = $this->requestStack->getCurrentRequest();

        if (null === $request) {
            return null;
        }

        // User info from OAuth headers
        $userId = $request->headers->get('X-User-Id');
        $userName = $request->headers->get('X-User-Email');

        if (null === $userId) {
            return null;
        }

        return new User($userId, $userName ?? 'unknown');
    }
}
```

#### 🔀 Combining Multiple Sources

```php
<?php

namespace App\Audit;

use App\Security\ApiTokenManager;
use DH\Auditor\User\User;
use DH\Auditor\User\UserInterface;
use DH\Auditor\User\UserProviderInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Security\Core\Authentication\Token\Storage\TokenStorageInterface;

class CompositeUserProvider implements UserProviderInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly TokenStorageInterface $tokenStorage,
        private readonly ApiTokenManager $apiTokenManager,
    ) {}

    public function __invoke(): ?UserInterface
    {
        // Try Symfony security first
        $token = $this->tokenStorage->getToken();
        if (null !== $token && null !== $token->getUser()) {
            $user = $token->getUser();
            return new User(
                method_exists($user, 'getId') ? (string) $user->getId() : '',
                $user->getUserIdentifier()
            );
        }

        // Fall back to API token
        $apiToken = $this->apiTokenManager->getCurrentToken();
        if (null !== $apiToken) {
            return new User(
                $apiToken->getClientId(),
                'API: ' . $apiToken->getClientName()
            );
        }

        return null;
    }
}
```

---

### 🚀 Next Steps

- 🧭 [Blame Context](blame-context.md) - Record how a change was made (import, command, Messenger message…)
- 🔒 [Security Provider](security-provider.md) - Customize IP/context detection
- 🛡️ [Role Checker](role-checker.md) - Customize access control

## Upgrade Guide (Auditor-bundle)

> **Navigate between major versions of auditor-bundle**

This section contains upgrade guides for major versions.

### 📚 Upgrade Guides

- ⬆️ [Upgrading to 8.0](v8.md) - From 7.x to 8.0
- ⬆️ [Upgrading to 7.0](v7.md) - From 6.x to 7.0

### 📋 Version Support

| Version | Status                 | Support Until |
|:--------|:-----------------------|:--------------|
| 8.x     | Active development 🚀  | Current       |
| 7.x     | Bug and security fixes | Until next major |
| 6.x     | End of Life            | -             |

### ✅ General Upgrade Process

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Always follow these steps when upgrading:

1. 📖 **Read the upgrade guide** for your target version
2. 📦 **Update dependencies** in `composer.json`
3. 🔄 **Run Composer update**
4. 🗑️ **Clear cache**
5. ⚙️ **Update configuration** if needed
6. ✅ **Run tests**

```bash
# Update dependencies
composer update damienharper/auditor damienharper/auditor-bundle

# Clear cache
bin/console cache:clear

# Run tests
bin/phpunit
```

### 🗄️ Schema Updates

After upgrading, always check if audit tables need updating.

**For fresh installations or existing v2 tables:**

```bash
# Preview changes
bin/console audit:schema:update --dump-sql

# Apply changes
bin/console audit:schema:update --force
```

**When upgrading from auditor-bundle 7.x or earlier (existing audit data):**

> [!CAUTION]
> `audit:schema:update` refuses to run if any audit table still has the legacy v1 schema. Run `audit:schema:migrate` first to preserve your data, then run `audit:schema:update`.
> The migration drops the legacy columns and cannot be undone: back up the audit tables, stop writing audits
> while it runs, and follow the [8.0 upgrade steps](v8.md#-upgrade-steps) in their order.

```bash
# Migrate legacy audit tables to v2 (converts the existing entries, then drops the legacy columns)
bin/console audit:schema:migrate --force --convert-all

# Then apply any remaining schema changes
bin/console audit:schema:update --force
```

## Upgrading to 7.0

> **Migrate from auditor-bundle 6.x to 7.0**

This guide covers upgrading from auditor-bundle 6.x to 7.0.

### 📋 Requirements Changes

#### PHP

| 6.x    | 7.0    |
|--------|--------|
| >= 8.2 | >= 8.4 |

#### Symfony

| 6.x    | 7.0    |
|--------|--------|
| >= 5.4 | >= 8.0 |

7.3 raised the minimum to Symfony 8.1.

> [!CAUTION]
> Symfony 5.4, 6.x, and 7.x are **no longer supported**.

#### Doctrine

| Package        | 6.x     | 7.0    |
|----------------|---------|--------|
| DBAL           | >= 3.2  | >= 4.0 |
| ORM            | >= 2.13 | >= 3.2 |
| DoctrineBundle | >= 2.0  | >= 3.0 |

#### auditor Library

| 6.x    | 7.0    |
|--------|--------|
| >= 3.0 | >= 4.0 |   

> [!TIP]
> See [auditor upgrade guide](https://github.com/DamienHarper/auditor/blob/master/UPGRADE-4.0.md) for library-specific changes.

#### PHPUnit

| 6.x     | 7.0     |
|---------|---------|
| >= 11.0 | >= 12.0 |

### 🔧 Bundle Changes

#### AbstractBundle Migration

The bundle now extends `Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Bundle\AbstractBundle` instead of `Bundle`.

This is an internal change and doesn't affect your configuration.

#### 🗑️ Removed Classes

| Removed Class                                                                            | Reason                                               |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `DH\AuditorBundle\DependencyInjection\Configuration`                                     | Merged into `DHAuditorBundle::configure()`           |
| `DH\AuditorBundle\DependencyInjection\DHAuditorExtension`                                | Merged into `DHAuditorBundle::loadExtension()`       |
| `DH\AuditorBundle\DependencyInjection\Compiler\AddProviderCompilerPass`                  | No longer needed with autowiring                     |
| `DH\AuditorBundle\DependencyInjection\Compiler\CustomConfigurationCompilerPass`          | Merged into bundle                                   |
| `DH\AuditorBundle\DependencyInjection\Compiler\DoctrineProviderConfigurationCompilerPass` | Replaced by `DoctrineMiddlewareCompilerPass`        |

#### 🗑️ Removed Files

- `src/Resources/config/services.yaml` - Services defined programmatically

#### Composer Scripts

The following composer scripts have been removed:
- `setup5` (Symfony 5.4)
- `setup6` (Symfony 6.4)
- `setup7` (Symfony 7.x)
- `setup8` (Symfony 8.0)

Use the new unified `setup` script instead:
```bash
composer setup
```

### 🚀 Upgrade Steps

#### 1️⃣ Update PHP

Ensure you have PHP 8.4+:

```bash
php -v
# PHP 8.4.x ...
```

#### 2️⃣ Update Symfony

```bash
composer require symfony/framework-bundle:^8.0
```

#### 3️⃣ Update Doctrine

```bash
composer require \
    doctrine/dbal:^4.0 \
    doctrine/orm:^3.2 \
    doctrine/doctrine-bundle:^3.0
```

#### 4️⃣ Update auditor

```bash
composer require damienharper/auditor:^4.0
```

#### 5️⃣ Update auditor-bundle

```bash
composer require damienharper/auditor-bundle:^7.0
```

#### 6️⃣ Clear Cache

```bash
bin/console cache:clear
```

#### 7️⃣ Check Schema

```bash
bin/console audit:schema:update --dump-sql
```

#### 8️⃣ Run Tests

```bash
bin/phpunit
```

### ⚙️ Configuration

No configuration changes required. Your `dh_auditor.yaml` should work as-is.

### ⚠️ Breaking Changes

#### auditor Library Changes

This bundle requires `damienharper/auditor` >= 4.0 which introduces several breaking changes.

##### Namespace Rename: Annotation → Attribute

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The `Annotation` namespace has been renamed to `Attribute` to align with PHP 8+ terminology.

```php
// Before (auditor 3.x)
use DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\Auditing\Annotation\Auditable;
use DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\Auditing\Annotation\Ignore;

// After (auditor 4.0)
use DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\Auditing\Attribute\Auditable;
use DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\Auditing\Attribute\Ignore;
```

##### `utf8_convert` is now opt-in

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The implicit `mb_convert_encoding()` pass that ran on every audit entry has been **removed from the default path**.

In auditor 3.x, UTF-8 conversion ran automatically. In auditor 4.0 it defaults to `false` because DBAL 4 enforces UTF-8 connections on PHP 8.4+, making the conversion a no-op for virtually all modern applications.

If your application handles data from legacy non-UTF-8 sources, re-enable it explicitly:

```yaml
# config/packages/dh_auditor.yaml
dh_auditor:
    providers:
        doctrine:
            utf8_convert: true
```

##### Entry Model - Property Hooks (PHP 8.4)

The `Entry` model now uses PHP 8.4 property hooks. Getter methods have been replaced by direct property access:

```php
// Before (auditor 3.x)
$entry->getId();
$entry->getType();
$entry->getObjectId();
$entry->getUserId();
$entry->getUsername();
$entry->getCreatedAt();

// After (auditor 4.0)
$entry->id;
$entry->type;
$entry->objectId;
$entry->userId;
$entry->username;
$entry->createdAt;
```

> [!TIP]
> See [auditor UPGRADE-4.0.md](https://github.com/DamienHarper/auditor/blob/master/UPGRADE-4.0.md) for the complete list of changes.

#### Route Names

The viewer route names have been updated for consistency:

| Before (6.x)                       | After (7.0)                          |
|------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| `dh_auditor_show_entity_history`   | `dh_auditor_show_entity_stream`      |
| `dh_auditor_show_transaction`      | `dh_auditor_show_transaction_stream` |

Update any route references in your code:

```php
// Before
$url = $urlGenerator->generate('dh_auditor_show_entity_history', [...]);

// After
$url = $urlGenerator->generate('dh_auditor_show_entity_stream', [...]);
```

#### Viewer Routes and `routing.controllers`

Up to 7.3.0, the bundle controllers were autoconfigured, so the `routing.controllers` resource of the
symfony/routing recipe (`config/routes.yaml`, Symfony 7.4+) could load the viewer routes instead of the
`auditor` route loader: with the default layout, where `config/routes.yaml` is imported last, they answered
at `/audit` whatever the prefix of your import, and they were registered even with the viewer disabled.
As of 7.3.1, they come from the `auditor` loader only:

- the prefix of your import applies: with `prefix: /admin` and the default layout, the viewer moves from
  `/audit` to `/admin/audit`; adapt your `access_control` rules and links;
- a disabled viewer (`viewer: false`) registers no route;
- an application that only got the viewer through `routing.controllers` must import the bundle routes
  (see [Route Configuration](../viewer/index.md#route-configuration)).

#### ConsoleUserProvider

CLI commands now use the command name as the user identifier instead of a generic `"command"` string:

| Before (6.x)                | After (7.0)                        |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `id: "command"`             | `id: "app:import-users"`           |
| `username: "app:import-users"` | `username: "app:import-users"` |

This allows filtering audit entries by specific CLI command in the viewer.

> [!NOTE]
> Existing audit entries with `blame_id = "command"` will not be automatically migrated.

#### Template Blocks

The following Twig blocks have been removed from the base layout:

| Removed Block        | Reason                           |
|----------------------|----------------------------------|
| `navbar`             | Replaced by built-in header      |
| `breadcrumbs`        | No longer used                   |

**Available blocks in 7.0:**

| Block                | Description                          | Available in                     |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `title`              | Page title                           | All pages                        |
| `stylesheets`        | CSS includes                         | All pages                        |
| `dh_auditor_content` | Main content area                    | All pages                        |
| `dh_auditor_header`  | Sub-header with back link & filters  | Entity stream, Transaction view  |
| `dh_auditor_pager`   | Pagination                           | Entity stream                    |
| `javascripts`        | JavaScript includes                  | All pages                        |

If you override `layout.html.twig` and use any of the removed blocks, update your template accordingly.

#### UserProvider

The `AnonymousToken` handling was removed (deprecated in Symfony 6.0).

**Before (6.x):**
```php
if ($token instanceof AnonymousToken) {
    return null;
}
```

**After (7.0):**
Anonymous tokens no longer exist in Symfony 8.0.

#### Custom Providers

If you have custom providers extending bundle classes, verify they still work.

The provider interfaces from the `auditor` library haven't changed:

- `UserProviderInterface`
- `SecurityProviderInterface`
- `RoleCheckerInterface`

#### PHP Attributes Migration

The bundle now uses modern PHP 8.4+ and Symfony 8+ attributes for service auto-configuration:

| Class | Change |
|-------|--------|
| `ConsoleEventSubscriber` | Uses `#[AsEventListener]` instead of `EventSubscriberInterface` |
| `ViewerEventSubscriber` | Uses `#[AsEventListener]` instead of `EventSubscriberInterface` |
| `TimeAgoExtension` | Uses `#[AsTwigFilter]` instead of extending `AbstractExtension` |
| `RoutingLoader` | Uses `#[AutoconfigureTag('routing.loader')]` attribute |

#### 🔒 Final Classes

> [!CAUTION]
> The following classes are now `final` and cannot be extended:

```php
// These classes can no longer be extended
DH\AuditorBundle\Event\ConsoleEventSubscriber
DH\AuditorBundle\Event\ViewerEventSubscriber
DH\AuditorBundle\Twig\TimeAgoExtension
DH\AuditorBundle\Routing\RoutingLoader
DH\AuditorBundle\User\UserProvider
DH\AuditorBundle\User\ConsoleUserProvider
DH\AuditorBundle\Security\SecurityProvider
DH\AuditorBundle\Security\RoleChecker
DH\AuditorBundle\Viewer\ActivityGraphProvider
```

If you were extending any of these classes, you'll need to use composition instead of inheritance.

#### ActivityGraphProvider API Changes

`ActivityGraphProvider` now uses PHP 8.4 property hooks with asymmetric visibility:

```php
// Before (6.x)
$days = $provider->getDays();
$layout = $provider->getLayout();

// After (7.0)
$days = $provider->days;
$layout = $provider->layout;
```

#### SecurityProvider

`SecurityProvider` now uses `#[Autowire]` attribute for dependency injection. This is an internal change but may affect you if you were manually constructing this service.

### 🔧 Troubleshooting

#### Class Not Found

If you get class not found errors for removed classes, you may have code referencing internal bundle classes. Update to use public APIs only.

#### Configuration Errors

Clear cache and warmup:

```bash
bin/console cache:clear
bin/console cache:warmup
```

#### Schema Issues

Check and update audit tables:

```bash
bin/console audit:schema:update --dump-sql
bin/console audit:schema:update --force
```

### ❓ Need Help?

- Check [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamienHarper/auditor-bundle/issues)
- Open a new issue with details about your error

---

## Upgrading to 8.0

> **Migrate from auditor-bundle 7.x to 8.0**

This guide covers upgrading from auditor-bundle 7.x to 8.0.

### ⚠️ DoctrineProvider extraction completed in auditor 5.0

`auditor-bundle` 8.0 targets `damienharper/auditor` 5.x, in which the embedded
`DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine` namespace has been **fully removed** from the core library.

All Doctrine ORM functionality now lives exclusively in
[`damienharper/auditor-doctrine-provider`](https://github.com/DamienHarper/auditor-doctrine-provider),
which auditor-bundle already requires as a direct dependency.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The class namespace **has not changed**. Classes are still under `DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\*`
> — they simply come from the `auditor-doctrine-provider` package instead of the `auditor` core.
> Only two imports change: the deprecated attribute aliases (see [Attributes](#attributes)) and
> [`NeedsConversionToAuditableType`](#needsconversiontoauditabletype-if-applicable).

#### Attributes

The deprecated 4.x aliases `DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\Auditing\Attribute\Auditable`, `Ignore` and `Security`
have been removed (only `AttributeLoader` remains in that namespace). Import the attributes from `DH\Auditor\Attribute`:

```php
// Before (deprecated aliases, auditor 4.x)
use DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\Auditing\Attribute\Auditable;
use DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\Auditing\Attribute\Ignore;
use DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\Auditing\Attribute\Security;

// After
use DH\Auditor\Attribute\Auditable;
use DH\Auditor\Attribute\Ignore;
use DH\Auditor\Attribute\Security;
```

#### For auditor-bundle users

No action required for the extraction. The bundle automatically requires `damienharper/auditor-doctrine-provider`
and wires everything transparently. Your `dh_auditor.yaml` configuration continues to work
without any changes. Your existing audit tables, however, must be migrated: see
[Audit Table Schema Reform](#-audit-table-schema-reform-schema-version-2) below.

#### For users using DoctrineProvider directly (without the bundle)

If you use `DoctrineProvider` directly in a non-bundle project, install the standalone package
explicitly:

```bash
composer require damienharper/auditor-doctrine-provider:^2.0
```

The provider imports remain identical:

```php
// Works in both 4.x (from auditor core) and 5.x (from auditor-doctrine-provider)
use DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\DoctrineProvider;
use DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\Configuration;
use DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\Persistence\Reader\Reader;
// ...
```

#### `NeedsConversionToAuditableType` (if applicable)

If you implemented the `NeedsConversionToAuditableType` interface on a custom Doctrine type,
update the import:

```php
// Before (auditor 4.x)
use DH\Auditor\Transaction\NeedsConversionToAuditableType;

// After (auditor 5.x / auditor-doctrine-provider 2.x)
use DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\Transaction\NeedsConversionToAuditableType;
```

### ⚠️ Audit Table Schema Reform (schema version 2)

auditor-bundle 8.0 also ships `damienharper/auditor-doctrine-provider` 2.x, which introduces a
**revised audit table schema**. The new schema:

- Replaces four separate `blame_*` columns with a single `blame JSON` column
- Replaces the SHA-1 `transaction_hash VARCHAR(40)` with a ULID `transaction_id CHAR(26)`
- Adds a `schema_version` column to distinguish legacy and current diffs formats
- Adds a `transaction_id` index and two composite indexes, `(object_id, type)` and `(blame_id, created_at)`,
  and drops the 7.x `(blame_user, blame_id)` index
- Unifies the `diffs` JSON format across all operation types

Existing audit tables are **not modified automatically**: they must be migrated with `audit:schema:migrate`,
which converts the existing entries, then drops the legacy columns. **There is no rollback**: back up the audit
tables first. Count 3 to 5 minutes per million audit rows, during which the application must not write audits.

### 🚀 Upgrade Steps

The complete procedure, with the backup, the rehearsal and the estimate of the duration, the options of
`audit:schema:migrate` and troubleshooting, is in the
[auditor-doctrine-provider 2.0 upgrade guide](https://github.com/DamienHarper/auditor-doctrine-provider/blob/main/docs/upgrade/v2.md#-upgrade-steps).
In short, and in this order:

#### 1️⃣ Back up the audit tables and rehearse

Back up every audit table, then run the whole procedure on a copy of your production data: it tells you how
long the maintenance window must be.

#### 2️⃣ Stop writing audits

Put the application in maintenance mode, and stop the Messenger workers and scheduled tasks (including the audit
retention): neither 7.x nor 8.0 can write audits into a table during its migration.

#### 3️⃣ Update auditor-bundle

```bash
composer require damienharper/auditor-bundle:^8.0
bin/console cache:clear
```

This will automatically pull in `damienharper/auditor:^5.0` and
`damienharper/auditor-doctrine-provider:^2.0`.

> [!CAUTION]
> Do not run `doctrine:schema:update`, nor a Doctrine migration that changes the audit tables, before step 4:
> on v1 tables, they drop the legacy columns without converting their data. If your audit tables are created by
> Doctrine migrations (test and CI databases, new environments, a deployment that migrates when it starts), see
> [Audit tables managed by Doctrine Migrations](https://github.com/DamienHarper/auditor-doctrine-provider/blob/main/docs/upgrade/v2.md#audit-tables-managed-by-doctrine-migrations):
> a replayable migration and a deployment order.

#### 4️⃣ Migrate the audit tables

```bash
# Preview the DDL
bin/console audit:schema:migrate --dump-sql --convert-all

# Run the full migration in one pass (new columns, transaction hash and diffs conversions, legacy columns dropped)
bin/console audit:schema:migrate --force --convert-all
```

> [!WARNING]
> Always pass `--convert-all`: `--force` alone adds the new columns, moves the blame into `blame` and drops the legacy
> `blame_*` and `ip` columns, but `transaction_hash` and the legacy diffs stay, and the tables stay on the legacy
> schema (`audit:schema:update` keeps refusing them) until the conversions have run.
> `--drop-transaction-hash` drops `transaction_hash` without converting it: the migrated entries lose their
> transaction grouping for good.

#### 5️⃣ Apply the rest of the schema

`audit:schema:update` refuses to run while an audit table still has the legacy v1 schema: run it only now.

```bash
bin/console audit:schema:update --dump-sql
bin/console audit:schema:update --force
```

#### 6️⃣ Check, then reopen

`audit:schema:migrate` must report that all audit tables are at schema version 2, and
`audit:schema:update --dump-sql` that there is nothing to update. Open a few entries in the viewer, then restart
the workers and scheduled tasks, and leave maintenance mode.

### 🔄 Breaking Changes (schema v2)

**`$entry->transactionHash` removed — use `$entry->transactionId`**

```php
// Before (7.x)
$entry->transactionHash;    // SHA-1 VARCHAR(40)

// After (8.0)
$entry->transactionId;      // ULID CHAR(26)
```

The old property has been **removed** (no deprecated alias). Update any code that accesses
`transactionHash` directly. For un-migrated v1 rows, `Entry::fromArray()` automatically
falls back to the legacy `transaction_hash` column so `$entry->transactionId` is still
populated before your tables are migrated.

**Blame properties now read from `blame` JSON column**

`$username`, `$userFqdn`, `$userFirewall`, and `$ip` still work — they now read from the unified
`blame` JSON column. No code changes required.

**User provider and impersonation**

- The built-in `UserProvider` no longer appends `[impersonator <name>]` to the username: the impersonated user is
  blamed, and the user who impersonates them is written in the `impersonator` key of the `blame` JSON
  (`$entry->impersonator`, `ImpersonatorFilter`, an "impersonated by" badge in the viewer). Exports get the
  `blame_impersonator_id`, `blame_impersonator` and `blame_impersonator_fqdn` fields.
- `user_fqdn` is the class of the user of the security token (it was `DH\Auditor\User\User`). Custom user
  providers pass it as the third argument of `User`: `new User($id, $name, DoctrineHelper::getRealClassName($user))`
  (`DH\Auditor\Provider\Doctrine\Persistence\Helper\DoctrineHelper` resolves Doctrine proxies).
- Existing entries are not rewritten. To find the ones written with the former suffix:

```sql
-- MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite
SELECT * FROM post_audit WHERE JSON_EXTRACT(blame, '$.username') LIKE '%[impersonator %';
-- PostgreSQL
SELECT * FROM post_audit WHERE CAST(blame AS jsonb) ->> 'username' LIKE '%[impersonator %';
```

**Remove entries can include a full entity snapshot**

For schema version 2 entries, `getDiffs()` on a `remove` entry is empty by default: `getDiffSource()` identifies the
deleted entity. With the provider option `full_snapshot_on_remove: true` (under `providers.doctrine`), it returns the
full entity state before deletion, with `old` populated and `new` set to `null` for every field.

**`getDiffSource()` available on all entry types**

Use `getDiffSource()` to access the entity metadata (`id`, `class`, `label`, `table`) that is
now present on all operation types in schema version 2.

### ✨ New Features

None of these features exists in 7.x. They are all optional: a 7.x configuration keeps working unchanged.

#### Viewer

- **Actions told as phrases** (*alice changed Status: Draft → Published*), with their technical details one click
  away, on new screens: an overview with the recent activity, the history of an object and of the entities attached
  to it, an action page, and the actions of a user. See [Pages](../viewer/index.md#-pages).
- **Compare two revisions** of an object, field by field, from its history. See
  [Compare Revisions](../viewer/index.md#compare-revisions-auditentityidcompare).
- **New filters**: who, what, field, origin and period on the history of an object; changed field (needs native JSON
  and a migrated table) and date range on the stream of an entity. The entity list can be sorted by name, number of
  actions or latest activity.
- **Schema v2 diffs**: removals can show the full state of the deleted object (`full_snapshot_on_remove`), JSON deep
  diffs get a dedicated rendering, and [diff label resolvers](../customization/diff-label-resolvers.md)
  (`#[DiffLabel]`) show readable values, wired by their FQCN as service ID.
- **URL generator**: `DH\AuditorBundle\Viewer\AuditViewerUrlGenerator` and its Twig functions link an entity, an object, a
  transaction or a user to its page in the viewer. See [Generating URLs](../viewer/index.md#-generating-urls).
- The user filter is computed from the `blame_id` index, which keeps the stream fast on large audit tables.
- **Strict Content Security Policy**: no inline script nor `style` attribute any more. See
  [Content Security Policy](../viewer/index.md#-content-security-policy).

#### Export

`/audit/export` streams audit entries as NDJSON, JSON or CSV, filtered by entity, object, period or user, optionally
anonymized, and restricted to the entities the user can view. See [Export](../viewer/index.md#-export).

#### Initial snapshot: `audit:snapshot`

When auditing is enabled on a database that already holds data, run `audit:snapshot` once: it writes an
`insert` entry flagged as a snapshot for every existing entity (in batches, skipping the entities that already
have an audit history), so their history starts with their state at that time.

```bash
php bin/console audit:snapshot --all --dry-run   # count what would be written
php bin/console audit:snapshot --all
```

The command is registered by the bundle. The viewer tells these entries as snapshots (a `SNAPSHOT` badge on the compare page), and
`Entry::isSnapshot()` tells them from real insertions in your own code.

#### `audited_columns` and `ignored_columns_resolver`

`entities.*.audited_columns` audits only the listed properties (allowlist), and `ignored_columns_resolver` takes the
ID of a service returning the properties to ignore for a given entity object. Ignoring always wins over the
allowlist. See [Configuration](../configuration/index.md#ignored_columns_resolver).

#### Histories across entities

`#[AuditRoot]` and the `roots` entity option attach the audit entries of an entity to the history of another one
(the `audit_root` table, `audit:roots:rebuild`); `Reader::createRootQuery()` reads that history with cursor
pagination. `root_resolver`, `entity_label_resolver` and `read_scope` take service IDs, field labels come from the
`dh_auditor_fields` translation domain, and the `dh_auditor_last_change()`, `dh_auditor_last_changes()` and
`dh_auditor_field_label()` Twig functions tell who changed a field. See [Histories](../customization/histories.md).
The `|dh_auditor_phrase`, `|dh_auditor_phrase_text` and `|dh_auditor_author` Twig filters tell an action as a
readable phrase whose objects link to their history, customizable through the `dh_auditor_history` translation
domain, `#[AsChangeDescriber]` services and the `ObjectUrlResolverInterface` service. See
[Phrases](../customization/histories.md#-phrases).

#### Blame contexts

Audit entries can record *how* a change was made in the `via` key of the `blame` JSON (no schema change):

- every console command runs in a `console` context labelled with the command name;
- the opt-in `dh_auditor.messenger.blame_context_middleware` blames the changes made by a worker on the user who
  dispatched the message;
- your code can push its own contexts through the autowirable `DH\Auditor\Blame\BlameContextStack` service;
- the viewer shows the context next to the author, and exports carry it as `blame_via` (see [Export](#export)).

See [Blame Context](../customization/blame-context.md).

#### Scheduled retention

Audit entries can be pruned on a schedule with Symfony Scheduler, per entity (`retention.max_age` /
`retention.max_entries`, or `#[Auditable(maxAge: …, maxEntries: …)]`), with an optional default. Disabled by default;
it needs `symfony/scheduler`, `symfony/messenger` and `dragonmantank/cron-expression`. See
[retention](../configuration/index.md#retention).

#### Doctrine provider options

The `providers.doctrine` options of auditor-doctrine-provider 2.0 are available:

- [`batch_size`](../configuration/index.md#batch_size): writes the audit entries of a transaction with multi-row
  `INSERT` statements (10 to 67 % faster flushes with many entities);
- [`compression`](../configuration/index.md#compression): compressed `diffs` and `extra_data` columns on MariaDB;
- [`skip_disabled_entities`](../configuration/index.md#skip_disabled_entities): no audit table for entities that
  are disabled by default;
- [`full_snapshot_on_remove`](../configuration/index.md#full_snapshot_on_remove): `remove` entries record the last
  value of every audited field.

#### Extensibility

- [Custom providers](../customization/custom-provider.md) are registered with the `dh_auditor.provider` tag.
- The console user provider can be decorated: decorate the `DH\AuditorBundle\User\ConsoleUserProvider` service
  with your own `DH\AuditorBundle\User\ConsoleUserProviderInterface` implementation.
- Failures that cannot be thrown (e.g. audit rows left behind after a rollback) are logged, on the `auditor` channel
  with MonologBundle.

### 🔄 Other Changes

**Entity `ignored_columns` of `#[Auditable]` entities are applied**

In 7.x, the attributes of an `#[Auditable]` entity replaced its whole YAML entity options (except retention): the
entity `ignored_columns` set in YAML were silently dropped. They are now added to the `#[Ignore]` properties, as
documented. Check that the properties listed there are really meant to be ignored.

**Viewer templates rewritten**

The templates of the viewer were rewritten around actions (see [Override Templates](../viewer/index.md#override-templates)):
a template overridden from 7.x under `templates/bundles/DHAuditorBundle/Audit/` no longer receives the same
variables and must be rewritten from the new one. In particular:

- `audits.html.twig` (now the overview) receives `activity` and counts actions instead of entries, in its activity
  graph too (`activityGraphRaw`; the `audit.audit_details.events_count` translation is removed);
- `entity_stream.html.twig` only renders the stream of a whole entity: the history of an object is
  `object_history.html.twig`, whose period filter is `when` (last days) instead of `date_from` / `date_to`;
- `transaction_stream.html.twig` renders one action (`row`, `entries`), no longer paginated;
- `user_stream.html.twig` receives `rows` (actions) instead of `entries`;
- `entry.html.twig` is removed: `compare.html.twig` renders its changes like the action details, with the
  `text_change()` and `related()` macros of `History/_macros.html.twig`.

The templates are styled with design tokens (see [Theme](../viewer/index.md#-theme)) instead of the Tailwind
palette, and every Tailwind class carries the `dh:` prefix (`dh:bg-dh-card`, `dh:text-dh-muted-foreground`,
`dh:hidden dh:sm:inline`…): the viewer never meets the classes of an application that uses Tailwind too, whatever the
order of the stylesheets. The precompiled `app.css` only holds the prefixed classes of the bundle templates, so an
overridden template that keeps 7.x classes (`slate-*`, `indigo-*`, `emerald-*`…) or unprefixed ones loses their
styles: rewrite it with prefixed classes and the tokens.

`app.css` no longer resets the whole page: its reset only reaches the content of the viewer pages, under the
`<div data-dh-auditor-viewer>` element in which each page of `Audit/` now wraps the content of its `dh_auditor_content`
block (keep it in an overridden page), and the `<twig:DhAuditor:History>` component. The layout of the bundle loads
`bundles/dhauditor/preflight.css` too; a [custom layout](../viewer/index.md#custom-layout) that extends the one of the
application only loads `app.css`, before or after its own stylesheets, and the rest of its page keeps their reset and
font. The wrapping element makes the content of each page one child of the element that renders the `dh_auditor_content`
block, which a flex or grid layout around it may need to know. An application that compiles the viewer or the
`<twig:DhAuditor:History>` component with its own Tailwind does it in a stylesheet of its own that imports `viewer.css`
with the `dh` prefix (see [Styling](../customization/histories.md#styling)).

The route names and their path parameters are unchanged, but the history of an object (`/audit/{entity}/{id}`) reads
other query parameters: `type` became `what`, `user` became `who`, `date_from` / `date_to` became `when` (last 7, 30
or 90 days), `page` became the `after` cursor, and `origin` and `attached` are new. Links built with the
`AuditViewerUrlGenerator` (or `dh_auditor_entity_url()`) get `type` and `user` translated; links written by hand with
the 7.x filters lose them.

**Overridden `layout.html.twig`: load `viewer.js`**

The theme toggle, the sort of the entity list and the filters submitted on change moved from inline scripts to
`bundles/dhauditor/viewer.js`. A layout that does not extend the bundle's one must load it (see
[Custom Layout](../viewer/index.md#custom-layout)); templates overridden from 7.x keep their inline scripts and work
as before, outside a strict CSP.

**Flushes made before the provider is built are audited** (also in 7.3)

The auditing listeners are declared as lazy Doctrine listeners of the connections of the auditing entity managers,
instead of being attached when the `DoctrineProvider` service is built. Before this fix, with a warm metadata cache
(the usual production setup), nothing built the provider before `kernel.controller`: the flushes made earlier in a web
request (a `form_login` / `json_login` listener updating the user, a `kernel.request` listener) were not audited.

This needs every auditing entity manager to be a DoctrineBundle one, using the event manager of its connection.
Otherwise the provider keeps attaching the listeners when it is built, as before, and the container compilation log
(`var/cache/<env>/*Compiler.log`) says which entity manager prevents it.

When the listeners are declared this way, workarounds that built the `Auditor` service before the first flush, so
that writes made before any controller (a firewall listener, a `kernel.request` listener) were audited, are no longer
needed: a Doctrine `preFlush` listener that only injects `Auditor`, for example, can be removed. Check first that the
container compilation log does not report an entity manager that prevents it.

### ❓ Need Help?

- Check [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamienHarper/auditor-bundle/issues)
- Open a new issue with details about your error

---

## Audit Viewer

> **Web interface for browsing audit logs**

The bundle includes a web interface for browsing audit logs.

### ✨ Enabling the Viewer

```yaml
# config/packages/dh_auditor.yaml
dh_auditor:
    providers:
        doctrine:
            viewer: true
```

Or with options:

```yaml
dh_auditor:
    providers:
        doctrine:
            viewer:
                enabled: true
                page_size: 50
```

### 🛤️ Routes

The viewer registers these routes:

| Route                                | URL                                | Description                         |
|--------------------------------------|------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `dh_auditor_export`                  | `/audit/export`                    | Export of audit entries (streamed)  |
| `dh_auditor_list_audits`             | `/audit`                           | List all audited entities           |
| `dh_auditor_show_entity_stream`      | `/audit/{entity}/{id?}`            | Entity audit stream                 |
| `dh_auditor_show_transaction_stream` | `/audit/transaction/{hash}`        | Transaction details                 |
| `dh_auditor_show_user_stream`        | `/audit/user/{id}`                 | Activity timeline of one user       |
| `dh_auditor_select_revisions`        | `/audit/{entity}/{id}/revisions`   | Pick two revisions of an object     |
| `dh_auditor_compare_revisions`       | `/audit/{entity}/{id}/compare`     | Compare two revisions of an object  |

#### Route Configuration

With Symfony Flex, routes are auto-configured. Otherwise, create `config/routes/dh_auditor.yaml`:

```yaml
dh_auditor:
    resource: "@DHAuditorBundle/Controller/"
    type: auditor
```

The viewer routes come from this import only, so its prefix applies to all of them. With `prefix: /admin`, the
viewer answers at `/admin/audit`:

```yaml
dh_auditor:
    resource: "@DHAuditorBundle/Controller/"
    type: auditor
    prefix: /admin
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The `routing.controllers` resource of the symfony/routing recipe (`config/routes.yaml`) does not load the viewer routes: an
> application that imports only `routing.controllers` has no viewer. Import the bundle routes as above.

### 📄 Pages

The viewer tells each action (a database transaction) as a phrase, such as *alice changed Status: Draft → Published
and added to Tags: symfony and audit*, with its technical details one click away. The phrases come from the
[history phrases](../customization/histories.md#-phrases): translate or describe them to speak the words of your
application. The objects they name link to their history, and are marked *(deleted)* when they no longer exist (when
their identifier is an integer or a string; an object hidden by a Doctrine SQL filter, such as a soft delete, is
marked as well).

#### Overview (`/audit`)

- **Recent activity**: the last 10 actions across the audited entities the reader may view, with what they were done
  on (*alice on Post “Why audit?”: …*). An action touching many objects is summed up by type (*deleted 38 Post*); it
  is read whole, whatever the number of its entries (a page reads 1,000 entries at most: past that, the largest
  actions tell only their most recent entries).
- **What is audited**: the audited entities (their name from the `dh_auditor_fields` domain, key FQCN), their number of
  actions (as their stream counts them, cached with the activity graph when its cache is on and no `read_scope` is
  set), their latest activity and, when enabled, their [activity graph](#-activity-graph). The list can be sorted by
  name, number of actions or latest activity (`?sort=name_asc`, `name_desc`, `count_desc`, `count_asc`,
  `activity_desc`, `activity_asc`).

#### Object History (`/audit/{entity}/{id}`)

The history of one object and of the entities attached to it (`#[AuditRoot]`, `roots` entity option, see
[Histories](../customization/histories.md)), newest first, grouped by day:

- one row per action: icon, author (linked to their actions), phrase, time, origin (Web, Command line, Messenger,
  System), blame context and, when the author was impersonated (switch user), who impersonated them; the whole row
  leads to the action page, the objects it names to their own history; its details list every change with its raw field and values (long texts compared word by word; a text shows between
  quotes only when it would be misread without them: empty, with spaces at its ends, or looking like a number, a
  boolean or null), the transaction and the blame, and link to the action page;
- **filters**: who, what (`insert`, `update`, `remove`, `associate`, `dissociate`), field (needs native JSON
  search), origin (`http`, `console`, `messenger`, `system`), when (last 7, 30 or 90 days), and, when entities can
  be attached, with or without them;
- **Show older actions** reads the next `page_size` actions through a cursor (`?after=`): a link, which `viewer.js`
  loads in place; the header counts the actions of the history;
- **Who changed what last**: the 8 fields changed most recently, with who changed them and when (or *at creation*);
- **Technical side**: class, identifier, audit tables read, number of entries.

```
/audit/App-Entity-Post/42?who=12&what=update&field=status
/audit/App-Entity-Post/42?origin=console&when=30&attached=0
```

Only the `view` role of the object's class is checked: its history shows the entries of the attached entities even
to a reader who cannot view their class (their links to their own history are hidden).

#### Entity Stream (`/audit/{entity}`)

Every action on an entity, with the filters of the stream: type, user (`__anonymous__` for the entries without
user), changed field, and period.

> [!NOTE]
> The changed field filter requires native JSON support (MySQL 5.7+, MariaDB 10.2.3+, PostgreSQL 9.4+, SQLite 3.38+) and an audit table migrated to the schema v2 structure (`audit:schema:migrate`). It is hidden otherwise. On large audit tables, combine it with a period: the database has to read the diffs of every entry left by the other filters.

```
/audit/App-Entity-User?type=update&user=42
/audit/App-Entity-User?type=insert&user=__anonymous__
/audit/App-Entity-User?field=email
/audit/App-Entity-User?date_from=2026-01-01&date_to=2026-03-31
```

The dates are days, inclusive, in the `dh_auditor.timezone` time zone. Filters are kept by the pager.

Pages hold `page_size` actions (transactions), whatever their number of entries: every page but the last holds as
many actions, each one whole. A page reads 1,000 entries at most: past that, the small actions stay whole and the
largest ones share the rest, each telling only its most recent entries. The header counts the actions the filters keep,
and a page beyond the last one shows the last one. The actions of a page are found by grouping the entries the filters
keep by transaction in the database: on a large audit table, a filter (type, user, period) keeps that cheap.

#### Action (`/audit/transaction/{hash}`)

One action: its phrase, the list of what it did, then every entry it wrote (up to 200), with its table and id, raw
fields and values, the transaction (and the date of its ULID), the blame and the raw diffs, which can be copied as
JSON. Opened from the history of an object (`?root=App\Entity\Post:42`), it links to the previous and next
actions of that history.

#### Actions of a User (`/audit/user/{id}`)

Everything a user did, across the audited entities the reader may view, newest first, each action with what it was
done on (*On Post “Why audit?”: …*), with filters on the entity (`on`), the type (`what`) and the period (`when`). The user is identified by the
`blame_id` recorded with each entry (up to 255 characters).

- Anonymous entries (no `blame_id`) have no page. Neither do entries recorded with an empty `blame_id`, which is what
  happens when the Symfony user class has no `getId()` method.
- Pages hold `page_size` actions, as in the entity stream: an action that wrote in several audit tables is one
  action, shown and counted once (the audit tables of one connection are read in one statement).

#### Compare Revisions (`/audit/{entity}/{id}/compare`)

From the history of an object, **Compare two states** lists its revisions: pick two of them to see the state of the
object before and after the changes made between them, field by field. The page links to the previous and next
revisions, so that the comparison can be moved along the history.

### 📤 Export

`/audit/export` streams audit entries, so that large exports do not load everything in memory:

| Parameter   | Description                                                                  |
|-------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `format`    | `ndjson` (default, recommended for large exports), `json` or `csv`           |
| `entity`    | Entity to export (`App-Entity-User`); all the entities the user can view when omitted |
| `id`        | Object ID                                                                    |
| `from`, `to`| Creation date range (ISO 8601, e.g. `2026-01-01`)                            |
| `blame_id`  | User ID                                                                      |
| `anonymize` | `1` to remove the user (ID, name, class, firewall, impersonator) and the IP address |

```
/audit/export?entity=App-Entity-User&format=csv&from=2026-01-01
```

Each entry carries the blame as flat fields: `blame_id`, `blame_user`, `blame_user_fqdn`, `blame_user_firewall`,
`blame_impersonator_id`, `blame_impersonator` and `blame_impersonator_fqdn` (the user who impersonated the author, if
any), `ip` and `blame_via`.

The export follows the same access rules as the viewer (see [Access Control](#-access-control)): an entity the user
cannot view is refused, or left out when no entity is given. From the command line, the provider's `audit:export`
command offers the same filters.

### 📊 Activity Graph

Each entity card displays a visual sparkline graph showing audit activity over time: one bar per day, the number of
actions (database transactions) of that day, as the stream of the entity counts them on that day. A bar leads to that
stream.

#### Configuration

```yaml
dh_auditor:
    providers:
        doctrine:
            viewer:
                enabled: true
                activity_graph:
                    enabled: true       # Show/hide the graph (default: true)
                    days: 30            # Number of days to display (default: 30, max: 30)
                    layout: 'bottom'    # Graph layout: 'bottom' or 'inline' (default: 'bottom')
                    cache:
                        enabled: true   # Enable caching (default: true)
                        pool: 'cache.app'  # Cache pool service ID
                        ttl: 300        # Cache TTL in seconds (default: 300)
```

#### Layout Options

| Layout   | Description                                                       |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `bottom` | Sparkline displayed below the entity info, full width (default)  |
| `inline` | Compact sparkline displayed in the header row, next to the number of actions |

#### Caching

The activity graph uses caching to improve performance on large audit tables. The number of actions shown for each
entity on the audit index page is counted as the entity stream counts them, and cached with the graph (same lifetime
and tag): a count may lag behind by up to the cache lifetime, as the graph does. Without the activity graph, or with
its cache disabled, the actions are counted on every page load.

With a `read_scope`, the graph and the number of actions count only the actions the scope lets the reader see, and are
never cached: the scope depends on the reader (a tenant, for instance), so they are computed on every page load.

> [!NOTE]
> Caching requires `symfony/cache`:
> ```bash
> composer require symfony/cache
> ```
> If `symfony/cache` is not installed, the graph will still work but without caching.

##### Cache with Tags

If your cache pool supports tags (`TagAwareCacheInterface`), the bundle uses the tag `dh_auditor.activity` for efficient cache invalidation.

#### 🗑️ Clear Cache Command

Clear the activity graph cache manually:

```bash
# Clear all activity graph cache
php bin/console audit:cache:clear

# Clear cache for a specific entity
php bin/console audit:cache:clear --entity="App\Entity\User"
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Clearing all cache requires a cache pool that supports tags. If your cache pool doesn't support tags, you can only clear cache for specific entities.

#### Display Behavior

| State                            | Behavior                                         |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Graph disabled (`enabled: false`)| Activity graph section is completely hidden      |
| Graph enabled, no data           | Placeholder with "No recent activity" message    |
| Graph enabled, with data         | Bars are normalized (tallest bar = 100%)         |

### 🎨 Theme

The viewer follows the conventions of [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com) without depending on it: every color of its
templates is a CSS variable, exposed to Tailwind as a `dh-*` color (`dh:bg-dh-card`, `dh:text-dh-muted-foreground`,
`dh:border-dh-input`…). The palette is neutral and the primary button near black; the teal of the auditor logo marks the activity
bars, the selected revision and the focus ring (`dh-brand`), and, darkened to read as text, the links, the time of an
action and the current page (`dh-link`). The icon of an action tells its meaning: green for a creation, red for a
deletion, blue for any other change. Controls share one size (`dh:h-8`, `dh:rounded-lg`), badges are pills (`dh:h-5`).

Every Tailwind class of the templates carries the `dh:` prefix (`dh:hidden`, `dh:sm:inline`, `dh:hover:bg-dh-accent`…),
and the theme variables of Tailwind in `bundles/dhauditor/app.css` are `--dh-*` ones (`--dh-spacing`, `--dh-text-sm`…):
none of them meets a class or a variable of an application that uses Tailwind too, whatever the order of the
stylesheets on the page.

The tokens live in `src/Resources/assets/css/theme.css`, already compiled into `bundles/dhauditor/app.css`:

| Token                                         | Role                                             |
|-----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `--dh-background`, `--dh-foreground`          | Page                                             |
| `--dh-card`, `--dh-card-foreground`           | Cards, tables                                    |
| `--dh-primary`, `--dh-primary-foreground`     | Primary button (Apply), checkboxes               |
| `--dh-muted`, `--dh-muted-foreground`         | Table headers, icons, secondary text             |
| `--dh-accent`, `--dh-accent-foreground`       | Hovered and selected rows                        |
| `--dh-border`, `--dh-input`, `--dh-ring`      | Borders, control borders, focus ring             |
| `--dh-brand`, `--dh-brand-from`, `--dh-brand-to` | Teal of the logo (bars, selection), its gradient |
| `--dh-deleted`, `--dh-inserted` (+ `-foreground`) | Removed and added text in the diffs          |
| `--dh-warning` (+ `-foreground`, `-border`)   | Notices of the comparison page                   |
| `--dh-link`, `--dh-link-foreground`           | Links, the clickable time of an action, current page |
| `--dh-create`, `--dh-update`, `--dh-delete` (+ `-foreground`) | Icon of an action by its meaning     |

Redefine any of them to restyle the viewer, after the bundle stylesheet (for instance in a stylesheet block of an
overridden `layout.html.twig`):

```css
:root { --dh-primary: #4f46e5; --dh-brand: #4f46e5; }
.dark { --dh-primary: #a5b4fc; --dh-brand: #a5b4fc; }
```

### 🌙 Dark Mode

The viewer includes a dark/light mode toggle button in the header. The dark values of the tokens apply under a `dark`
class on an ancestor, set on `<html>` by `viewer.js`.

#### Behavior

- **Default**: Follows system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`)
- **Manual toggle**: Click the sun/moon icon in the header
- **Persistence**: User preference is saved in `localStorage`

The toggle works without page reload and persists across sessions.

### 🔐 Content Security Policy

The viewer carries no inline script, event handler attribute nor `style` attribute: its behaviours (theme, sort of
the entity list, filters submitted on change, technical mode, copy of the raw diffs, older actions loaded in place)
live in `bundles/dhauditor/viewer.js`, loaded by `layout.html.twig`, and
its styles in `bundles/dhauditor/app.css` and `bundles/dhauditor/preflight.css`. It therefore works under a strict policy such as
`script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'`, as long as the bundle assets are served from your origin
(`bin/console assets:install`).

### 🔒 Access Control

#### Via Configuration

```yaml
dh_auditor:
    providers:
        doctrine:
            entities:
                App\Entity\User:
                    roles:
                        view:
                            - ROLE_ADMIN
```

#### Via Attributes

```php
#[Audit\Auditable]
#[Audit\Security(view: ['ROLE_ADMIN'])]
class User {}
```

#### Via Symfony Security

```yaml
# config/packages/security.yaml
security:
    access_control:
        - { path: ^/audit, roles: ROLE_ADMIN }
```

The rule must match the path the viewer is imported at: with `prefix: /admin`, write `^/admin/audit`.

> [!WARNING]
> When neither the entity nor its scope requires roles, the default role checker grants the viewer to every visitor.
> Protect the imported path with an `access_control` rule (or a firewall) unless the audits are meant to be public.

> [!NOTE]
> In association diffs (`associate` / `dissociate`), the related entity links to its audit stream
> only when the current user can open it: the entity must be audited and its `view` roles granted.
> Otherwise it is displayed as plain text. Templates can apply the same rule with the
> `dh_auditor_is_viewable(entity)` Twig function (an entity object or class name).

### 🔗 URL Format

Entity namespaces use dashes instead of backslashes:

```
App\Entity\User → App-Entity-User
```

Helper methods:

```php
use DH\AuditorBundle\Helper\UrlHelper;

// Namespace to URL parameter
$param = UrlHelper::namespaceToParam('App\Entity\User');
// Returns: 'App-Entity-User'

// URL parameter to namespace
$namespace = UrlHelper::paramToNamespace('App-Entity-User');
// Returns: 'App\Entity\User'
```

### 🔧 Generating URLs

Link your own pages to the viewer with the `AuditViewerUrlGenerator` service (autowirable) or its
Twig functions. They hide the route names and parameters of the viewer, and the encoding of the
entity class in its URLs.

#### Twig

```twig
{# Audit stream of an entity: an object, or a class name with an optional id #}
<a href="{{ dh_auditor_entity_url(post) }}">History</a>
<a href="{{ dh_auditor_entity_url('App\\Entity\\Post') }}">All posts</a>
<a href="{{ dh_auditor_entity_url('App\\Entity\\Post', 42, {what: 'update'}) }}">Updates of post #42</a>

{# Transaction and user timeline #}
<a href="{{ dh_auditor_transaction_url(entry.transactionId) }}">Transaction</a>
{# ... opened from the history of post #42: the action page offers its previous and next actions #}
<a href="{{ dh_auditor_transaction_url(entry.transactionId, root: 'App\\Entity\\Post:42') }}">Transaction</a>
<a href="{{ dh_auditor_user_url(entry.userId) }}">User activity</a>

{# Absolute URL, e.g. in an email #}
{{ dh_auditor_entity_url(post, absolute: true) }}
```

Each function returns `null` when the viewer cannot show the page: viewer disabled, auditor
disabled, entity not audited, entity not persisted yet, or an entry without user (anonymous change) or without
transaction id. Access rights are not checked: combine
the link with `dh_auditor_is_viewable()` to show it only to users allowed to open it.

```twig
{% set history_url = dh_auditor_entity_url(post) %}
{% if history_url and dh_auditor_is_viewable(post) %}
    <a href="{{ history_url }}">History</a>
{% endif %}
```

#### PHP

```php
use DH\AuditorBundle\Viewer\AuditViewerUrlGenerator;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Generator\UrlGeneratorInterface;

public function __construct(private AuditViewerUrlGenerator $auditUrls) {}

// Audit stream of an entity object (its identifier is read from the entity)
$url = $this->auditUrls->generateEntityUrl($post);

// Audit stream of a class, of one object, with viewer filters
$url = $this->auditUrls->generateEntityUrl(Post::class);
$url = $this->auditUrls->generateEntityUrl(Post::class, 42, ['what' => 'update', 'who' => '42']);

// Absolute URL
$url = $this->auditUrls->generateEntityUrl($post, referenceType: UrlGeneratorInterface::ABSOLUTE_URL);

// Transaction and user timeline
$url = $this->auditUrls->generateTransactionUrl($entry->transactionId);
$url = $this->auditUrls->generateUserUrl($entry->userId);
```

The filters are the query parameters of the page: `type`, `user`, `field`, `date_from`, `date_to` and `page` for
the stream of an entity; `what`, `who`, `field`, `origin`, `when` and `attached` for the history of an object, which
gets the `type` and `user` filters as `what` and `who`. The identifier of an entity object is converted like the `object_id` stored in
the audit table (UUID, enum, custom type), and a Doctrine reference is not loaded to read it.

### 🎨 Customization

#### Override Templates

Create files in `templates/bundles/DHAuditorBundle/`:

```
templates/bundles/DHAuditorBundle/
├── Audit/
│   ├── audits.html.twig              # Overview
│   ├── object_history.html.twig      # History of an object
│   ├── entity_stream.html.twig       # Stream of an entity
│   ├── transaction_stream.html.twig  # Action
│   ├── user_stream.html.twig         # Actions of a user
│   ├── revisions.html.twig           # Revisions of an object
│   ├── compare.html.twig             # Comparison of two revisions
│   └── helpers/
│       ├── helper.html.twig          # Helper macros
│       └── pager.html.twig           # Pagination
├── History/
│   ├── _actions.html.twig            # Actions grouped by day, and the link to older ones
│   ├── _row.html.twig                # One action
│   ├── _details.html.twig            # Technical details of an action
│   ├── _macros.html.twig             # Icons, origin badges, day headings, change rendering
│   ├── phrase.html.twig              # A phrase
│   └── object_reference.html.twig    # An object named by a phrase
├── Component/
│   └── History.html.twig             # <twig:DhAuditor:History> component
└── layout.html.twig                  # Base layout
```

> [!NOTE]
> The changeset of a JSON column is a deep diff: a tree whose leaves are `{new}`, `{old}` or `{new, old}`.
> A JSON object whose own keys are `new`/`old` therefore looks like a field diff, so a custom template must not
> tell them apart by their keys. Use `entry.isDeepDiff(field)` for the root of a changeset, and the
> `dh_auditor_is_diff_leaf(node)` Twig function for the nodes inside a deep diff.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> `bundles/dhauditor/app.css` only contains the classes of the bundle templates, with the `dh:` prefix. An overridden
> template styles itself with prefixed classes and the `dh-*` tokens (`dh:bg-dh-card`, see [Theme](#-theme)); a class
> without the prefix, or that no bundle template uses, such as the 7.x `bg-slate-50` or `text-indigo-600`, has no
> style. An overridden page of `Audit/` keeps the `<div data-dh-auditor-viewer>` element that wraps the content of
> its `dh_auditor_content` block: the reset of the viewer applies under it.

#### Custom Layout

```twig
{# templates/bundles/DHAuditorBundle/layout.html.twig #}
{% extends 'base.html.twig' %}

{% block stylesheets %}
    {{ parent() }}
    {# the viewer, with its own reset, bounded to its content: the rest of your page is left as it is #}
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ asset('bundles/dhauditor/app.css') }}">
    {# behaviours of the viewer (theme, sort, filters, technical mode, copy, older actions); loaded without defer so
       that the theme applies before the first paint #}
    <script src="{{ asset('bundles/dhauditor/viewer.js') }}"></script>
{% endblock %}

{% block body %}
    <div class="container">
        {% block dh_auditor_content %}{% endblock %}
    </div>
{% endblock %}
```

`bundles/dhauditor/app.css` holds the `dh:` classes of the viewer, its tokens and its controls. It may come before
or after the stylesheets of your application, which keeps its own classes, theme and font: the sans-serif text of the
viewer is the one of your page, only its code and a few signs use the stacks of the `--dh-font-mono` and
`--dh-font-sans` variables (`:root { --dh-font-sans: var(--font-sans); }` to change the latter). It does not reset
your page either: its reset, the one of Tailwind (Preflight) cut down to what the templates need, only reaches the
content of the pages of the viewer, under a `data-dh-auditor-viewer` element, so that the viewer looks the same with
or without a reset of your own. The layout of the bundle adds `bundles/dhauditor/preflight.css`, the whole Preflight
of Tailwind; a layout that extends yours does not need it.

> [!WARNING]
> The rules of the viewer sit in the cascade layers of Tailwind (`base`, `components`, `utilities`). A rule of your
> application outside any layer (Bootstrap, plain CSS such as `select { padding: … }`) wins over all of them on the
> elements it matches, whatever the order of the stylesheets. Put such rules in a layer, or scope them out of the
> viewer. An application that compiles the viewer itself (see [Styling](../customization/histories.md#styling))
> does not load `app.css` as well.

#### Template Blocks

| Block                | Description                          | Available in                     |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `title`              | Page title                           | All pages                        |
| `stylesheets`        | CSS includes                         | All pages                        |
| `dh_auditor_content` | Main content area                    | All pages                        |
| `dh_auditor_header`  | Sub-header with back link & filters  | Entity stream, revisions, comparison |
| `dh_auditor_pager`   | Pagination                           | Entity stream, revisions         |
| `javascripts`        | JavaScript includes                  | All pages                        |      

### 📦 Assets

Install assets:

```bash
bin/console assets:install
```

Assets are installed to `public/bundles/dhauditor/`: `app.css` (the viewer), `preflight.css` (the reset of
Tailwind, loaded by the layout of the bundle only) and `viewer.js` (its behaviours).

### 🌍 Translations

Available translations:

| Language   | Code |
|------------|------|
| English    | `en` |
| French     | `fr` |
| German     | `de` |
| Spanish    | `es` |
| Italian    | `it` |
| Dutch      | `nl` |
| Russian    | `ru` |
| Ukrainian  | `uk` |
| Estonian   | `et` |

The viewer uses your application's locale automatically.

### 🚫 Disabling the Viewer

```yaml
dh_auditor:
    providers:
        doctrine:
            viewer: false
```

Routes are not registered, `/audit` returns 404.
